timing_rule: Latest earlier calendar year per source within 3 years; retain all same-year question variants.

same_sex_marriage.support_definition: Support for allowing same-sex couples to marry legally / agreement with their right to marry; wording and denominators remain source-specific.

cases.name: Baker v. Nelson
cases.coverage_note: Not found in the current serving index by case name; no vote count inferred from the unsigned order.
cases.interpretation_limit: Summary dismissal has limited merits effect on the issues necessarily decided, unlike a standing dismissal. It does not adopt every rationale below. See Mandel v. Bradley, 432 U.S. 173, 176 (1977): https://www.law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/432/173 . Baker was later overruled in Obergefell Part III.

components.issue: Challenge to exclusion from marriage licensing
components.decision: Appeal dismissed for want of a substantial federal question.
components.scope: Summary disposition left the challenged Minnesota judgment in place; not a new nationwide legislative prohibition.
components.locator: 409 U.S. 810, October 10, 1972, docket 71-1027; PDF page 10. Obergefell Part III discusses and overrules Baker.
components.survey_fit: Broad licensing-policy direction is comparable in principle, but this survey selection has no eligible pre-1972 observation.

cases.name: Hollingsworth v. Perry

components.decision: No standing; Ninth Circuit judgment vacated, appeal to be dismissed
components.scope: Article III appellate jurisdiction, not adjudication of whether states must permit same-sex marriage
components.evidence: the case is remanded with instructions to dismiss the appeal for lack of jurisdiction
components.survey_fit: Do not assign a policy-agreement score from marriage-legality responses

cases.practical_effect: The district-court injunction against enforcement of Proposition 8 was left undisturbed; distinguish that consequence from a Supreme Court merits endorsement of marriage equality.
cases.roster_evidence: Syllabus author/joiner paragraph; Kennedy dissent heading
cases.interpretation_limit: The dissent concerns standing; it must not be coded as opposition to marriage equality.

cases.name: United States v. Windsor

components.issue: Federal recognition of lawful same-sex marriages
components.scope: Federal treatment of marriages lawful under state law; not a nationwide state licensing requirement
components.locator: Majority Part IV, final two paragraphs; syllabus holding 2
components.evidence: This opinion and its holding are confined to those lawful marriages.
components.survey_fit: Broad marriage-legality preference is directionally relevant context, not a direct measure of support for DOMA section 3 invalidation

observations.denominator: Support/oppose respondents only; harmonized missing answers excluded, original unsure/nonresponse categories unavailable here.

components.issue: Jurisdiction despite executive agreement with Windsor
components.scope: Jurisdiction component only; the separate DOMA holding does decide merits

cases.interpretation_limit: Votes and dissent authors are not measurements of the justices' personal approval of marriage equality.

components.decision: States must permit same-sex couples to marry on equal terms
components.evidence: The Court now holds that same-sex couples may exercise the fundamental right to marry.
components.survey_fit: Direct broad policy-direction comparison with allowing same-sex couples to marry; not approval of the constitutional reasoning

cases.interpretation_limit: An unsigned opinion does not supply a named majority-joinder roster. Broad marriage approval is not measured approval of this birth-certificate holding.

components.issue: Equal marital treatment on birth certificates
components.decision: Rejected unequal treatment of same-sex spouses under Arkansas birth-certificate rules.
components.scope: Application of equal marital benefits under Obergefell to the challenged birth-certificate treatment.
components.locator: Per curiam opening and closing paragraphs; dissent heading for author and joiners.
components.survey_fit: Marriage-legality questions provide broad context only. No selected item directly measures support for these birth-certificate rules.

limitations: Explicit source-based legal coding is an input, not an automated legal classifier.
Contextual matches do not measure approval of the specific holding.
Mixed and unresolved components retain their labels; no scalar direction is inferred.
No pooling, confidence intervals, causal claims, or prediction.
